items.title: Hypolite Charles Interview, 1963-04-13
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Alfred Williams; the interviewer mentions him as someone who talks about Henry Martin.

ctx.x: They criticized Red so much, those boys, about he couldn't play, you know. In other words, Red couldn't produce the good like some of them drummers, and they criticized him. So Red got hot and he just left. And first thing you know Red then the little, what do you call him, piano, I mean that violin

player. Welch. Welch. You know something I don't understand about Henry Martin now. You remember Alfred Williams, a drummer, he's always talking about how great Henry Martin was you know, and what a wonderful drummer he was. Why did he switch to banjo? No, no.

Henry Martin couldn't play no drums. No? No. He played the drum. You know a drummer, not to say talk about it, but a drummer, he's got to be fast. A drummer can't lag. A drummer can make you play music. Or you can play if you've got a drummer. That's right. Oh my goodness. That's why my band used to run. One Red was playing with me that was a dead band. But when Welch got in there, but look when we had the Maple Leaf band, Cantrell was playing in there. You talk about a drummer.
